doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Cuban-American community and where he lived
summary: The Cuban community in Union City was not helpful to a jazz career; he lived with his mother, then West New York, then Manhattan Plaza with soprano Brenda Feliciano.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The musical life was quite interesting, obviously for somebody who had just gotten there. Did you become involved in the Cuban American community in the New York area?

I In those days was starting to fade, I mean the minority… The dream of every Cuban, of most of the Cubans—except for my mother—is to migrate to Miami, but I made that contact here, Mario Bauza. Mario was like kind of waiting here for me; he was a friend of my father from the 30s and 40s, and um, Graciela and all of those guys, I contact them, but the Cuban community was not very helpful for my work, for the type of work I did, because I wanted to be a Jazz musician, and there was very few Cubans involved in that, as a community. They are, the Cuban community was more involved in Cuban music, or what they called the Salsa movement, but I had little to do.
There is a large Cuban American community around Union, New Jersey right?
Union City, in Union City, when I arrive there, the first, I live like for six or seven month in the heart of the Cuban community in Union City. My mother lived there for many
years on 38th St. They have a lot of Cuban restaurants and all that. It was a very vibrant community.
Union City is where you were living with your mother, when you first got to the U.S.?
Yea, in Union City. They have signs in the store that say, “We speak English.” [Both laugh]
Where did you wind up when you finally got on your own?

Later on we move to West New York which is like, 10 blocks from Union City. And then I met Brenda, a wonderful soprano, when I, when my marriage was destroyed, a Puerto Rican soprano called Brenda Feliciano. So we go together, and that happen almost 30 years ago. So I move to New York with her, to a building called Manhattan Plaza. Dexter Gordon used to live there and Adam Makowicz, the pianist. A lot of musicians used to live there. Neil Carter used to have an apartment around there. So was a very wonderful experience living there, all the musicians and actors and choreographers. It was wonderful living in the center of New York.
